translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenjin

translations.idiomatic: (Wencong, Xi, and Wenshou)

translations.literal: Xu Yougong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yougong

translations.idiomatic: (Shang Yanruo)

sentences.zh: 唐臨，字本德，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Tang Lin, style name Bende, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin, whose style name was Bende, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 周內史瑾之孫。

translations.literal: He was the grandson of Jin, Interior Secretary of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Jin, who had served Zhou as interior secretary.

sentences.zh: 其先自北海內徙。

translations.literal: His ancestors had moved inward from Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His family had earlier moved inland from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 武德初，隱太子討王世充，臨以策進說，太子引直典書坊，授右衛率府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, when the Hidden Crown Prince campaigned against Wang Shichong, Lin advanced stratagems and was brought in to serve straight in the Palace Library, and was appointed Army-Equipment Registrar in the Right Guard Commandant's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, when the Hidden Crown Prince marched against Wang Shichong, Lin offered strategic advice and was brought onto his staff in the Palace Library, then appointed registrar of army equipment in the Right Guard commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，出為萬泉丞。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he went out as magistrate of Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was deposed, he was sent out as magistrate of Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 有輕囚久系，方春，農事興，臨說令可且出囚，使就畎畝。

translations.literal: There were light offenders long detained; spring had come and farm work was rising, and Lin urged the magistrate that the prisoners might for the time be released to return to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Some minor offenders had been held a long time. With spring at hand and farming underway, Lin urged the magistrate to release them temporarily so they could work their fields.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate refused.

sentences.zh: 臨曰：「有所疑，丞執其罪。

translations.literal: Lin said: "If there is doubt, the aide bears the guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "If there is any doubt, the aide will bear the responsibility."

sentences.zh: 」令移疾，臨悉縱歸，與之約，囚如期還。

translations.literal: The magistrate reported illness, and Lin released them all, making an appointment with them; the prisoners returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate then pleaded illness, and Lin released them all on their promise to return; every prisoner came back on time.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 大夫韋挺責著位不肅，明日，挺越次與江夏王道宗語，臨進曰：「王亂班。

translations.literal: Senior Censor Wei Ting had rebuked someone for dress and position lacking solemnity; the next day Ting stepped out of rank to speak with Prince Daozong of Jiangxia, and Lin advanced and said: "The prince has disturbed the ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Senior censor Wei Ting had rebuked an official for failing to observe proper court decorum. The next day Ting himself stepped out of rank to converse with Prince Daozong of Jiangxia, and Lin stepped forward and said, "Your Highness has disturbed the ranks."

sentences.zh: 」道宗曰：「與大夫語，何至爾！

translations.literal: Daozong said: "Speaking with the senior censor—how does it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Daozong replied, "I am only speaking with the senior censor—why make so much of it!"

sentences.zh: 」臨曰：「大夫亦亂班。

translations.literal: Lin said: "The senior censor has also disturbed the ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "The senior censor has disturbed the ranks as well."

sentences.zh: 」挺失色，眾皆悚伏。

translations.literal: Ting changed color, and the crowd all shrank in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Ting turned pale, and everyone present shrank back in awe.

sentences.zh: 俄持節按獄交州，出冤系三千人。

translations.literal: Soon, bearing credentials, he reviewed cases in Jiaozhou and released three thousand persons wrongfully held.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was commissioned to review cases in Jiaozhou and released three thousand people who had been wrongfully imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗錄囚，臨占對無不盡，帝喜曰：「為國之要在用法，刻則人殘，寬則失有罪，惟是折中，以稱朕意。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong once reviewed prisoners; Lin's responses in every case were complete, and the emperor rejoiced and said: "The key to governing the state lies in applying the law: if harsh, men are maimed; if lenient, the guilty escape—only by striking the mean can it suit my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once held a prison review, and Lin answered every case without leaving anything unresolved. The emperor was pleased and said, "Governing a state depends on how the law is applied: if it is harsh, people are ruined; if it is lenient, the guilty go free. Only by striking the right balance can it satisfy my intent."

sentences.zh: 」它日復訊，余司斷者輒紛訴不已，獨臨所訊無一言。

translations.literal: Another day when cases were heard again, the other offices that judged kept appealing in confusion without end, but those Lin examined had not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: On another review day, prisoners judged by other officials kept appealing without end, but not one of those Lin had tried spoke up.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，答曰：「唐卿斷囚不冤，所以絕意。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason, and he answered: "Minister Tang's judgments of prisoners are not unjust, and so they have no further wish to speak."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why, and he answered, "Minister Tang's judgments are never unjust, so they have given up any thought of appealing."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘆曰：「為獄者固當若是。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "One who handles prisons ought indeed to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "A man who runs the prisons ought indeed to be like this."

sentences.zh: 」乃自述其考曰「形如死灰，心若鐵石」雲。

translations.literal: He then himself set forth his assessment, saying "form like dead ashes, heart like iron and stone."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote his own assessment of Lin: "His bearing is like dead ashes, his heart like iron and stone."

sentences.zh: 臨累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Lin was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was eventually promoted to minister of the civil office.

sentences.zh: 初，來濟謫臺州，李義府謫普州，臨奏許祎為江南巡察使，張倫劍南巡察使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lai Ji had been demoted to Taizhou and Li Yifu to Puzhou; Lin memorialized that Xu Yi be made Jiangnan inspection commissioner and Zhang Lun Jiannan inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lai Ji had been demoted to Taizhou and Li Yifu to Puzhou. Lin memorialized appointing Xu Yi as Jiangnan inspection commissioner and Zhang Lun as Jiannan inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 祎與濟善，而倫與義府有隙。

translations.literal: Yi was on good terms with Ji, while Lun had a rift with Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was friendly with Ji, whereas Lun bore a grudge against Yifu.

sentences.zh: 武後常右義府，察知之，謂臨遣所私督其過，坐免官。

translations.literal: Empress Wu often favored Yifu; perceiving this, she said Lin had sent his own men to watch for Yifu's faults, and on that charge he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu habitually favored Yifu. When she perceived this arrangement, she accused Lin of sending his own men to hunt for Yifu's faults, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 起為潮州刺史，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He was raised up as prefect of Chaozhou and died at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed prefect of Chaozhou and died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 臨儉薄寡欲，不好治第宅。

translations.literal: Lin was frugal and sparing in desire and did not like to build mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Lin lived frugally with few wants and never cared to build a fine residence.

sentences.zh: 性旁通，專務掩人過。

translations.literal: By nature he was broadly accommodating and devoted himself to covering others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was broad-minded and made a point of concealing others' faults.

sentences.zh: 見妻子，必正衣冠。

translations.literal: When he saw wife and children he always straightened cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Even when receiving his wife and children he always dressed in full formal attire.

sentences.zh: 兄皎，武德初，為秦王府記室，從王征討，掌書檄。

translations.literal: His elder brother Jiao, at the beginning of Wude, was recorder in the Prince of Qin's household, followed the prince on campaigns, and managed documents and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jiao, early in the Wude era, served as recorder in the Prince of Qin's household, accompanied the prince on campaign, and handled documents and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，官吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was vice minister of the civil office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he served as vice minister of the civil office.

sentences.zh: 先是，選集四時補擬，不為限。

translations.literal: Previously, selection assemblies for appointment were held in all four seasons without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, selection assemblies for appointments had been held in all four seasons without restriction.

sentences.zh: 皎請以冬初集，盡季春止，後遂為法。

translations.literal: Jiao requested that assemblies begin at the start of winter and end at the close of late spring, and afterward this became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao proposed that assemblies begin at the start of winter and end by late spring, and this afterward became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 終益州長史，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: He ended as chief administrator of Yizhou and was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as chief administrator of Yizhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 子之奇，給事中。

translations.literal: His son Zhiqi was a Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiqi served as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 坐章懷太子屬徙邊。

translations.literal: He was implicated as a follower of Crown Prince Zhanghuai and banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was implicated as an associate of Crown Prince Zhanghuai and banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後除括蒼令，與徐敬業起兵，誅。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed magistrate of Kuocang; he joined Xu Jingye in raising troops and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed magistrate of Kuocang, joined Xu Jingye's rebellion, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 臨孫紹紹，神龍時為太常博士。

translations.literal: Lin's grandson Shaoshao, in the Shenlong era, was an Erudite of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's grandson Shaoshao served in the Shenlong era as an erudite of the grand imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遷左臺侍御史、度支員外郎，常兼博士。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attending Censor of the Left Bureau and Vice Director of Revenue, and often concurrently held the erudite post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor of the left bureau and vice director of revenue, and often held the erudite post concurrently.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人請妃、公主、命婦以上葬給鼓吹，詔可。

translations.literal: Consort Wei requested that consorts, princesses, and titled ladies of rank and above be granted martial music at burial, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei requested that imperial consorts, princesses, and titled ladies of rank and above be granted martial music at burial, and the edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「鼓吹本軍容，黃帝戰涿鹿，以為警衛，故曲有《靈夔吼》、《雕鶚爭》、《石墜崖》、《壯士怒》之類。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Martial music is originally military regalia; when the Yellow Emperor fought at Zhuolu it served as guard and escort, and so its pieces include such titles as 'Spirit Kui Roars,' 'Eagle and Goshawk Contend,' 'Stone Falls from the Cliff,' and 'Bold Warrior's Wrath.'"
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Martial music was originally military regalia. When the Yellow Emperor fought at Zhuolu it served as guard and escort, which is why its pieces include titles such as 'Spirit Kui Roars,' 'Eagle and Goshawk Contend,' 'Stone Falls from the Cliff,' and 'Bold Warrior's Wrath.'"

sentences.zh: 惟功臣詔葬，得兼用之。

translations.literal: Only meritorious ministers buried by imperial decree might use it together with other rites.
translations.idiomatic: Only meritorious ministers granted burial by imperial decree were permitted to use it.

sentences.zh: 男子有四方功，所以加寵。

translations.literal: A man who had merit in the four directions was thereby given added favor.
translations.idiomatic: It was bestowed on men who had earned merit on all sides as a mark of special honor.

sentences.zh: 雖郊祀天地，不參設，容得接閨閫哉？

translations.literal: Even at suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth it was not set out together—how could it be joined to the inner quarters?
translations.idiomatic: Even at suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth it was not deployed alongside other rites—how then could it be extended to the women's quarters?

sentences.zh: 在令，五品官昏葬，無給鼓吹者，唯京官五品則假四品，蓋班秩在夫若子。

translations.literal: In the statutes, for the wedding burial of a fifth-rank official there was no grant of martial music; only a capital fifth-rank official borrowed fourth rank, because rank order followed husband or son.
translations.idiomatic: Under statute, fifth-rank officials were not granted martial music at burial. Only capital officials of fifth rank borrowed fourth-rank honors, because ceremonial rank followed that of husband or son.

sentences.zh: 請置前詔，用舊典。

translations.literal: He requested setting aside the recent edict and using the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the recent edict be set aside and the old regulations restored.

sentences.zh: 」不省。

translations.literal: It was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His plea went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 中宗始郊，國子祭酒祝欽明等知韋後能制天子，欲迎諂之，即奏以皇后亞獻，安樂公主終獻，又四時及列帝誕日，遣使者詣陵如事生。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong first performed suburban sacrifice, National University Rector Zhu Qinming and others, knowing that Consort Wei could control the Son of Heaven, wished to curry favor and at once memorialized that the empress perform the secondary offering and Princess Anle the final offering; moreover, in all four seasons and on the birth days of successive emperors, envoys were sent to the tombs as if they were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong first performed the suburban sacrifice, National University rector Zhu Qinming and others, knowing Consort Wei could dominate the emperor, sought to flatter her. They memorialized that the empress perform the secondary offering and Princess Anle the final offering, and that in all four seasons and on successive emperors' birthdays envoys be sent to the tombs as though the dead were still living.

sentences.zh: 紹以為非禮，引正誼固爭。

translations.literal: Shao regarded it as contrary to ritual and cited orthodox principle in firm opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Shao held these measures contrary to ritual propriety and argued against them on principle with unwavering firmness.

sentences.zh: 帝又詔武氏陵及諸武墓皆置守戶，紹謂：「昊、順二陵守戶五百，與昭陵同。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered guard households for the Wu clan tombs and all Wu graves; Shao said: "The tombs of Emperors Hao and Shun have five hundred guard households, the same as Zhaoling."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered guard households for the Wu clan tombs and all Wu family graves. Shao said, "The tombs of Emperors Hao and Shun have five hundred guard households, the same as Zhaoling."

sentences.zh: 在令，先世帝王陵戶二十，今雖崇奉外家，宜準附常典。

translations.literal: In the statutes, tombs of former dynasties' emperors and kings had twenty households; though the maternal kin are now honored, they should follow and attach to the usual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Under statute, tombs of former dynasties' emperors and kings have twenty guard households. Though the maternal kin are now honored, they should conform to the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 又親王墓戶十，梁、魯乃追贈，不可逾真王。

translations.literal: Moreover, princes' tombs had ten households; Liang and Lu were posthumous enfeoffments and could not exceed true princes.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' tombs have ten guard households. Liang and Lu were posthumous enfeoffments and cannot exceed true princes.

sentences.zh: 褒德衛卒，至逾宗廟，不可明甚，請罷之。

translations.literal: The guards honoring virtue at Wei's tomb went so far as to exceed the ancestral temple—it could not be clearer—and he requested abolishing them.
translations.idiomatic: The guard honoring virtue at Wei's tomb goes so far as to exceed what is due the ancestral temple. The impropriety could not be clearer. I ask that it be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「比群臣務厚葬，以俑人象驂眩耀相矜，下逮眾庶，流宕成俗。

translations.literal: He also said: "Recently ministers have pursued lavish burial, using figurines and images of outriders to dazzle and boast against one another, reaching down to the common people until it has become a drifting custom."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Recently officials have competed in lavish burials, using figurines and images of outriders to dazzle and outdo one another, a practice that has spread even among common people and become a widespread custom."

sentences.zh: 願按令切敕裁損，凡明器不許列衢路，惟陳墓所。

translations.literal: He wished that by statute a stern edict cut and reduce it: all spirit objects were not to be arrayed on public roads but only displayed at the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a strict edict be issued under statute to curb this excess: spirit objects must not be displayed along public roads but only at the grave site.

sentences.zh: 昏家盛設障車，擁道為戲樂，邀貨捐貲動萬計，甚傷化紊禮，不可示天下。

translations.literal: Wedding families lavishly set out barrier carts, blocking the road for sport and amusement, soliciting goods and donations running to tens of thousands—it greatly harmed transformation and disordered ritual and could not be shown to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wedding families lavishly deploy barrier carts, blocking the roads for spectacle and amusement and soliciting gifts and donations that run into tens of thousands. This gravely harms public morals and disrupts ritual order and must not be displayed before the realm.

sentences.zh: 」事雖不從，議者美嘆。

translations.literal: Though the matter was not followed, those who discussed it admired and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Though his proposals were not adopted, commentators praised him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，數言政損益，再遷給事中，兼太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly spoke on what would add or subtract in government and was again promoted to Supervising Secretary, concurrently Vice Minister of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly offered advice on improving government and was promoted again to supervising secretary, concurrently serving as vice minister of the grand imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，玄宗講武驪山，紹以典儀坐失軍容，當斬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, Xuanzong held military exercises at Lishan; Shao, as master of ceremonies, sat in neglect of military decorum and was liable to execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantian, when Xuanzong held military exercises at Lishan, Shao, as master of ceremonies, was charged with neglecting military decorum and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，執纛下，左右猶冀少貸，金吾將軍李邈遽傳詔斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and had him taken below the banner; those around him still hoped for slight leniency, but General of the Golden Crow Li Miao hastily transmitted the edict and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had him seized below the command banner. Those around him still hoped for some leniency, but General of the Golden Crow Li Miao hastily transmitted the edict and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 時深咎邈，帝亦悔，俄詔罷邈官，擯於家。

translations.literal: At the time they deeply blamed Miao; the emperor also repented, and soon an edict removed Miao from office and banished him to his home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many blamed Miao severely, and the emperor himself soon regretted the matter. Before long he issued an edict stripping Miao of office and banishing him to his home.

sentences.zh: 張文瓘，字稚圭，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenjin, style name Zhigui, was a man of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenjin, whose style name was Zhigui, came from Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，徙家魏州之昌樂。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye in Sui, the family moved to Changle in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui Daye era his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母、兄以孝友聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served mother and elder brother and was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he cared for his mother and elder brother and was known for filial devotion and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，第明經，補并州參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed military aide in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed military aide in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時李勣為長史，嘗嘆曰：「稚圭，今之管、蕭，吾所不及。

translations.literal: At the time Li Ji was chief administrator and once sighed and said: "Zhigui is today's Guan and Xiao—I cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Ji served as chief administrator and once sighed and said, "Zhigui is a Guan Zhong or Xiao He for our age—I cannot match him."

sentences.zh: 」勣入朝，文瓘與屬僚二人皆餞，勣贈二人以佩刀、玉帶，而不及文瓘。

translations.literal: When Ji entered court, Wenjin and two subordinate officials all saw him off; Ji gave the two a girdle knife and jade belt but did not include Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji went to court, Wenjin and two subordinate officials all saw him off. Ji gave the two men a girdle knife and a jade belt but gave Wenjin nothing.

sentences.zh: 文瓘以疑請，勣曰：「子無為嫌。

translations.literal: Wenjin asked out of doubt, and Ji said: "Sir, do not take offense."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin asked about the omission, and Ji said, "Do not take offense, sir."

sentences.zh: 若某，豫少決，故贈以刀，欲其果於斷；

translations.literal: As for a certain one, he is by nature slow to decide, so I give a knife, wishing him to be firm in judgment;
translations.idiomatic: One of them is by nature hesitant in judgment, so I gave him a knife, hoping he would learn to decide firmly;

sentences.zh: 某放誕少檢，故贈以帶，俾其守約束。

translations.literal: a certain one is unrestrained and lacking in restraint, so I give a belt, to make him keep discipline.
translations.idiomatic: the other is unrestrained and lax in conduct, so I gave him a belt to help him keep himself in check.

sentences.zh: 若子才，無施不可，焉用贈？

translations.literal: As for your talent, there is nothing it cannot be applied to—what use is a gift?
translations.idiomatic: As for your talent, there is nothing you cannot do well—what need is there for a gift?

sentences.zh: 」因極推引。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pushed his recommendation to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Wenjin to the fullest extent.

sentences.zh: 再遷水部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Director of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to vice director of waterways.

sentences.zh: 時兄文琮為戶部侍郎，於制，兄弟不並臺閣，出為雲陽令。

translations.literal: At the time his elder brother Wencong was vice minister of revenue; by regulation brothers did not serve together in the Secretariat, and he went out as magistrate of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his elder brother Wencong was vice minister of revenue. By regulation brothers could not serve together in the secretariat, so Wenjin was sent out as magistrate of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 累授東西臺舍人，參知政事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Secretariat Drafter of the Eastern and Western Bureaus and participated in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed secretariat drafter of the eastern and western bureaus and given a role in governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年，遷東臺侍郎、同東西臺三品，遂與勣同為宰相。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he was moved to Vice Director of the Eastern Bureau and Third Rank Equal to the Eastern and Western Bureaus, and thus with Ji became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfeng he was promoted to vice director of the eastern bureau with third rank equal to the eastern and western bureaus, and thus became chancellor alongside Ji.

sentences.zh: 俄知左史事。

translations.literal: Soon he was put in charge of left historiographer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of the left historiographer's office.

sentences.zh: 時高宗造蓬萊、上陽、合璧等宮，復征討四夷，京師養廄馬萬匹，帑瓘浸虛。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong built the Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi, and other palaces, again campaigned against the four barbarians, and in the capital kept ten thousand stable horses; the treasury stores gradually emptied.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozong was building the Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi, and other palaces, campaigning again against the frontier peoples, and maintaining ten thousand horses in the capital stables, while the treasury was steadily drained.

sentences.zh: 文瓘諫曰：「王者養民，逸則富以康，勞則怨以叛。

translations.literal: Wenjin remonstrated and said: "A king nourishes the people: if they are at ease they grow rich and secure; if they are toiled they grow resentful and rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin remonstrated, saying, "A ruler nourishes his people: when they are at ease they grow prosperous and secure; when they are overworked they grow resentful and rebel."

sentences.zh: 秦、漢廣事四夷，造宮室，至二世土崩，武帝末年戶口減半。

translations.literal: Qin and Han broadly engaged the four barbarians and built palaces, until the Second Emperor's collapse and in Emperor Wu's late years the registered population was halved.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han both lavished effort on the frontier peoples and built palaces on a vast scale, until the Qin collapsed in the reign of the Second Emperor and in Emperor Wu's late years the registered population was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 夫制治於未亂，保邦於未危。

translations.literal: Now, establish order before disorder, preserve the state before peril.
translations.idiomatic: Order must be established before chaos arises, and the state preserved before danger appears.

sentences.zh: 人罔常懷，懷於有仁。

translations.literal: The people have no constant heart—they rest their hearts on whoever has benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The people have no constant loyalty; they give their hearts to whoever shows benevolence.

sentences.zh: 臣願撫之，無使勞而生怨。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to comfort them and not let toil give rise to resentment.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty comfort them and not let overwork breed resentment.

sentences.zh: 隋監未遠，不可不察。

translations.literal: Sui's mirror is not far off—it cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of Sui is still close at hand and must not be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言，賜繒錦百段，為減廄馬數千。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, granted a hundred lengths of silk brocade, and reduced stable horses by several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice, granted him a hundred lengths of silk brocade, and reduced the stable herds by several thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 改黃門侍郎，兼太子右庶子，又兼大理卿。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Right Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and again concurrently Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the yellow gate, concurrently right vice guardian of the heir apparent, and again concurrently minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，斷疑獄四百，抵罪者無怨言。

translations.literal: In less than ten days he decided four hundred doubtful cases, and those punished had no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days he resolved four hundred doubtful cases, and not one of those punished lodged a complaint.

sentences.zh: 嘗有小疾，囚相與齋禱，願亟視事。

translations.literal: Once when he had a slight illness, prisoners together fasted and prayed, wishing him to resume duties quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he fell slightly ill, the prisoners together fasted and prayed that he would soon return to his duties.

sentences.zh: 時以執法平恕方戴胄。

translations.literal: At the time for impartial and lenient enforcement he was set beside Dai Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was ranked alongside Dai Zhou for impartial and lenient enforcement of the law.

sentences.zh: 後拜侍中，兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Palace Attendant, concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed palace attendant, concurrently guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 諸囚聞其遷，皆垂泣，其得人心如此。

translations.literal: When all prisoners heard of his transfer they wept; such was the measure of his winning hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When the prisoners heard of his transfer they all wept—such was the depth of regard he had won.

sentences.zh: 性嚴正，未嘗回容，諸司奏議，悉心糾駁，故帝委之。

translations.literal: By nature stern and upright, he never bent his countenance; on memorials from all offices he diligently corrected and refuted, and so the emperor entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and upright and never showed favoritism. On memorials from every office he scrutinized and corrected errors with care, and for this the emperor relied on him.

sentences.zh: 或時移疾，佗宰相奏事，帝必問與文瓘議未。

translations.literal: When at times he reported illness, if other chancellors presented business the emperor always asked whether it had been discussed with Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was ill, if other chancellors presented business the emperor always asked whether Wenjin had been consulted.

sentences.zh: 若不者，曰：「往共籌之。

translations.literal: If they had not, he would say: "Go plan it together with him."
translations.idiomatic: If they had not, he would say, "Go discuss it with him together."

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「已議。

translations.literal: Or someone would say: "It has already been discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Or they would say, "It has already been discussed."

sentences.zh: 」即皆報可。

translations.literal: Then all would report approval.
translations.idiomatic: Then all reported their approval.

sentences.zh: 新羅叛，帝將出兵討之。

translations.literal: Silla rebelled; the emperor was about to send troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Silla rebelled, and the emperor was preparing to send an army to punish them.

sentences.zh: 時文瓘病臥家，自力請見，曰：「吐蕃盜邊，兵屯境未解，新羅復叛，議者欲出師，二虜俱事，臣恐人不堪弊，請息兵修德，以懷異俗。

translations.literal: At that time Wenjin lay ill at home; exerting himself he requested an audience and said: "The Tibetans plunder the borders and troops remain massed on the frontier without having withdrawn; Silla has rebelled again and those deliberating wish to dispatch an army. With trouble from both barbarians at once, I fear the people cannot bear the strain. I beg that we rest the armies and cultivate virtue, so as to win over foreign peoples."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wenjin was ill and confined at home, but he forced himself to seek an audience and said, "The Tibetans are raiding our borders and troops are still stationed on the frontier without having been withdrawn. Silla has rebelled again, and those deliberating wish to send out an army. With both frontier foes engaged at once, I fear the people cannot bear the burden. I beg that we halt the armies and cultivate virtue, so as to win over foreign peoples by kindness."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 初，同列以堂饌豐余，欲少損。

translations.literal: Initially his colleagues, because the hall meals were plentiful, wished to reduce them somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At first his colleagues, finding the hall provisions abundant, wished to cut them back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 文瓘曰：「此天子所以重樞務、待賢才也，吾等若不任職，當自引避，不宜節減，以自取名。

translations.literal: Wenjin said: "This is how the Son of Heaven shows weight to pivot affairs and treats worthy talent. If we are not equal to our offices we should withdraw of ourselves; it is not fitting to cut and reduce in order to make a name for frugality."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin said, "This is how the Son of Heaven shows the weight of pivot affairs and treats worthy talent. If we are not equal to our duties we should withdraw on our own; it is not fitting to pare them down in order to win a reputation for thrift."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃止。

translations.literal: The others then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The others then stopped.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三，贈幽州都督，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-three; posthumously he was made Military Governor of Youzhou, with posthumous title Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three; posthumously he was made military governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Resolute.

sentences.zh: 以嘗事孝敬皇帝，詔陪葬恭陵。

translations.literal: Because he had once served the Filial and Respectful Emperor, an edict ordered his burial at Gong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had once served the Filial and Respectful Emperor, an edict ordered him buried at Gong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 四子：潛，為魏州刺史；

translations.literal: Four sons: Qian, who was prefect of Wei Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Qian, who was prefect of Wei Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 沛，同州刺史；

translations.literal: Pei, prefect of Tong Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Pei, prefect of Tong Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 洽，衛尉卿；

translations.literal: He, Minister of the Guard;
translations.idiomatic: He, minister of the guard;

sentences.zh: 涉，殿中監。

translations.literal: She, Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: She, director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父子皆至三品，時謂「萬石張家」。

translations.literal: Father and sons all reached the third rank; the age called them "the Zhang family of ten thousand piculs."
translations.idiomatic: Father and sons all reached the third rank; the age called them "the Zhang family of ten thousand piculs."

sentences.zh: 韋溫誅，涉為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Wei Wen was executed, She was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Wen was executed, She was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 文琮，好自寫書，筆不釋手。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved to copy books by his own hand and never laid down his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong loved to copy books himself and never put down his brush.

sentences.zh: 子弟諫止，曰：「吾好此，不為倦。

translations.literal: His sons and younger kin admonished him to stop; he said: "I delight in this and am not wearied."
translations.idiomatic: His sons and younger kin admonished him to stop, but he said, "I delight in this and am not wearied by it."

sentences.zh: 」貞觀中，為治書侍御史，遷亳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was Director of the Imperial Library on Punishments, then transferred to prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he served as director of the imperial library on punishments, then was transferred to prefect of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，獻《文皇帝頌》，優制褒美，拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he presented "A Eulogy to Emperor Wen" and received an excellent edict of praise; he was appointed vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yonghui he presented "A Eulogy to Emperor Wen," received an excellent edict of praise, and was appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 坐房遺愛從母弟，出為建州刺史。

translations.literal: Because he was a maternal cousin of Fang Yi'ai, he was sent out as prefect of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a maternal cousin of Fang Yi'ai, he was sent out as prefect of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州尚淫祀，不立社稷，文琮下教曰：「春秋二社本於農，今此州廢不立，尚何觀？

translations.literal: The prefecture still indulged licentious shrines and had not established the altars of soil and grain. Wenzong issued an instruction: "The spring and autumn twin sacrifices arise from agriculture; now this prefecture has abandoned them and not established them—what is there to behold?
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture still favored licentious cults and had not established the altars of soil and grain. Wenzong issued an instruction: "The spring and autumn twin sacrifices have their root in agriculture; now this prefecture has abandoned them and not set them up—what is there to look to?

sentences.zh: 比歲田畝卒荒，或未之思乎！

translations.literal: Fields in recent years end in desolation—has no one reflected on this!
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the fields have ended in desolation—has no one thought of this?

sentences.zh: 神在於敬，可以致福。

translations.literal: The spirits dwell in reverence; through it blessing may be attained.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits dwell in reverence; through reverence blessing may be attained.

sentences.zh: 」於是始建祀場，民悅從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first built the sacrifice grounds, and the people gladly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they first built the sacrifice grounds, and the people gladly followed.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子錫，久視初，為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，代其甥李嶠為宰相。

translations.literal: His son Xi: at the beginning of Jiushi he was Vice Director of Phoenix Pavilion and Associate Director of Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, with the status of Grand Councillor, succeeding his nephew Li Jiao as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi: at the beginning of the Jiushi era he was vice director of the phoenix pavilion and associate director of the phoenix pavilion and crane terrace, with the status of grand councillor, succeeding his nephew Li Jiao as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 請還廬陵王，不為張易之所右。

translations.literal: He requested the return of the Prince of Luling and did not yield to Zhang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for the return of the Prince of Luling and would not yield to Zhang Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 與鄭杲俱知選，坐泄禁中語，又賕謝鉅萬，時蘇味道亦坐事，同被訊，系鳳閣，俄徙司刑三品院。

translations.literal: Together with Zheng Gao he oversaw selection; he was convicted of divulging palace speech and also of accepting bribes in the tens of thousands. At the time Su Weidao was also implicated; both were questioned, detained at Phoenix Pavilion, and soon moved to the Third-Rank Courtyard of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zheng Gao he oversaw selection. He was convicted of divulging palace matters and also of accepting bribes in the tens of thousands. At the time Su Weidao was also implicated; both were interrogated, detained at the phoenix pavilion, and soon moved to the third-rank courtyard of the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 錫按轡專道，神氣不懾，日膳豐鮮，無損貶。

translations.literal: Xi held the reins on the exclusive track, his spirit undaunted; daily meals remained rich and fresh, without diminishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi rode holding the reins on the privileged lane, his bearing unshaken; his daily meals remained rich and fresh, without any curtailment.

sentences.zh: 味道徒步赴逮，席地菜食。

translations.literal: Weidao went on foot to his arrest and ate vegetables sitting on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao went on foot to his arrest and ate plain vegetables sitting on the ground.

sentences.zh: 武後聞之，釋味道，將斬錫，既而流循州。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu heard of it she released Weidao and was about to execute Xi, but in the end exiled him to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu heard of it she released Weidao and was about to execute Xi, but in the end exiled him to Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，累遷工部尚書，兼修國史，東都留守。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, concurrently revising the national history and left in charge of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to minister of works, concurrently revising the national history, and left in charge of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 韋後臨朝，詔同中書門下三品，旬日，出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei held court, an edict made him of the same rank as the Three Departments at the Secretariat and Chancellery; in ten days he was sent out as prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei held court, an edict made him of the same rank as the three departments at the secretariat and chancellery; within ten days he was sent out as prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累封平原郡公，卒。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed cumulatively as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery and died.

sentences.zh: 文琮從父弟文收，終太子率更令。

translations.literal: Wenzong's cousin on the father's side Wenshou, ended as Chief Commandant of Rate Revision for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's paternal cousin Wenshou ended as chief commandant of rate revision for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 善音律，著《新樂書》十餘篇。

translations.literal: Skilled in pitch and regulation; he authored more than ten chapters of "New Book of Music."
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in pitch and regulation, he authored more than ten chapters of the New Book of Music.

sentences.zh: 徐有功，名弘敏，避孝敬皇帝諱，以字行，國子博士文遠孫也。

translations.literal: Xu Yougong—his name Hongmin, avoiding the taboo of the Filial and Respectful Emperor, went by his style-name—was grandson of the Erudite of the Imperial Academy Xu Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yougong—his name Hongmin; to avoid the taboo of the Filial and Respectful Emperor he went by his style-name—was grandson of the erudite of the imperial academy Xu Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，累補蒲州司法參軍，襲封東莞縣男。

translations.literal: He passed the classics examination, was repeatedly appointed judicial administrator of Pu Prefecture, and inherited enfeoffment as Baron of Dongguan County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the classics examination, was repeatedly appointed judicial administrator of Pu Prefecture, and inherited enfeoffment as baron of Dongguan County.

sentences.zh: 為政仁，不忍杖罰，民服其恩，更相約曰：「犯徐參軍杖者，必斥之。

translations.literal: His governance was humane; he could not bear the birch rod. The people submitted to his kindness and made a pact among themselves: "Whoever would have Administrative Assistant Xu beaten must be driven out."
translations.idiomatic: His governance was humane and he could not bear the rod. The people submitted to his kindness and made a pact among themselves: "Whoever would have Administrative Assistant Xu flogged must be driven away."

sentences.zh: 」訖代不辱一人。

translations.literal: By the end of his tenure not a single person had been shamed.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of his tenure not a single person had been disgraced by beating.

sentences.zh: 累遷司刑丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 時武後僭位，畏唐大臣謀己。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Wu usurped the throne and feared that Tang grandees would plot against her.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Wu usurped the throne and feared that Tang grandees would plot against her.

sentences.zh: 於是周興、來俊臣、丘神勣、王弘義等揣識後指，置總監牧院諸獄，捕將相，俾相鉤逮，掩搦護送，楚掠凝慘。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wang Hongyi and others divined the empress's intent and set up the various prisons of the General Supervisor's Pasture Court; they seized generals and chancellors, made them implicate one another in arrests, covered and seized them for escort, and torture grew thick and ghastly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wang Hongyi, and others divined the empress's intent and established the various prisons of the general supervisor's pasture court. They seized generals and chancellors, made them implicate one another, covered and seized them for escort, and torture grew ever more cruel and ghastly.

sentences.zh: 又汙引天下豪桀，馳使者即按，一切以反論。

translations.literal: They also defiled and drew in the empire's bold spirits; they galloped envoys to investigate on the spot, and everything was judged as treason.
translations.idiomatic: They also defiled and implicated the empire's bold spirits, galloping envoys to investigate on the spot; everything was judged as treason.

sentences.zh: 吏爭以周內窮詆相高，後輒勸以官賞，於是以急變相告言者無虛日。

translations.literal: Officials vied to outdo one another in thoroughgoing slander within the circuits; the empress would then urge them on with offices and rewards—thus there was no day without urgent denunciations and mutual informing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials vied to outdo one another in exhaustive investigation and slander; the empress would then encourage them with offices and rewards—thus there was no day without urgent denunciations and mutual informing.

sentences.zh: 朝野震恐，莫敢正言，獨有功數犯顏爭枉直，後厲語折抑，有功爭益牢。

translations.literal: Court and countryside trembled in terror; none dared speak straight. Only Yougong repeatedly offended her countenance disputing wrong from right; the empress checked him with harsh words, yet Yougong argued all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside trembled in terror and none dared speak plainly. Only Yougong repeatedly offended her countenance to dispute wrong from right. The empress rebuked him with harsh words, yet Yougong argued all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 時博州刺史瑯邪王沖，責息錢於貴鄉，遣家奴督斂，與尉顏餘慶相聞知，奴自市弓矢還。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Langye, Wang Chong, as prefect of Bo, was collecting interest money at Gui Township and sent a household slave to press collection; he had exchanges with the Assistant Magistrate Yan Yuqing, and the slave returned from buying bows and arrows on his own.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Langye, Wang Chong, as prefect of Bo, was collecting interest money at Gui Township and sent a household slave to press for payment. He had exchanges with the assistant magistrate Yan Yuqing, and the slave returned after buying bows and arrows on his own.

sentences.zh: 會沖坐逆誅，魏州人告餘慶豫沖謀，後令俊臣鞫治，以反狀聞。

translations.literal: When Chong was executed for rebellion, men of Wei Prefecture reported that Yuqing had prefigured Chong's plot. The empress ordered Junchen to interrogate and investigate, and he reported the facts of treason.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong was executed for rebellion, men of Wei Prefecture reported that Yuqing had foreknown Chong's plot. The empress ordered Junchen to interrogate and investigate, and he reported the facts of treason.

sentences.zh: 有司議：「餘慶更永昌赦，法當流。

translations.literal: The relevant offices deliberated: "Yuqing falls again under the Yongchang amnesty; by law he should be banished."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices deliberated: "Yuqing again falls under the Yongchang amnesty; by law he should be banished."

sentences.zh: 」侍御史魏元忠謂：「餘慶為沖督償、通書，合謀明甚，非曰支黨，請殊死，籍其家。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Secretary Wei Yuanzhong said: "Yuqing for Chong pressed repayment and exchanged letters—the conspiracy is abundantly clear. He is not called a branch follower; I request extraordinary death and confiscation of his household."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance secretary Wei Yuanzhong said, "Yuqing for Chong pressed repayment and exchanged letters—the conspiracy is abundantly clear. He is not called a branch follower; I request extraordinary death and confiscation of his household."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 有功曰：「永昌赦令：『與虺貞同惡，魁首已伏誅，支黨未發者原之。

translations.literal: Yougong said: "The Yongchang amnesty order states: 'Those who shared evil with Hui Zhen—if the ringleaders have already been put to death, branch followers who have not yet been exposed are forgiven.'
translations.idiomatic: Yougong said, "The Yongchang amnesty order states: 'Those who shared evil with Hui Zhen—if the ringleaders have already been put to death, branch followers who have not yet been exposed are forgiven.'"

sentences.zh: 』《書》曰：『殲厥渠魁』，律以『造意為首』，尋赦已伏語，則魁首無遺。

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'Exterminate their leader'; the code takes 'the one who originated intent as chief.' Seeking the amnesty's words 'have already submitted,' then no ringleader remains.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, 'Exterminate their leader'; the code takes 'the one who originated the intent as chief.' If we follow the amnesty's words 'have already submitted,' then no ringleader remains.

sentences.zh: 餘慶赦後被言，是謂支黨。

translations.literal: Yuqing was spoken of after the amnesty—that is what is called a branch follower.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing was denounced after the amnesty—that is what is called a branch follower.

sentences.zh: 今以支為首，是以生入死。

translations.literal: Now to take a branch follower as the chief is to bring the living into death.
translations.idiomatic: Now to take a branch follower as the chief is to bring the living into death.

sentences.zh: 赦而復罪，不如勿赦；

translations.literal: Pardon and then punish again—better not to pardon;
translations.idiomatic: To pardon and then punish again would be better not to have pardoned at all;

sentences.zh: 生而復殺，不如勿生。

translations.literal: Give life and then kill again—better not to give life.
translations.idiomatic: to give life and then kill again would be better not to have given life at all.

sentences.zh: 竊謂朝廷不當爾。

translations.literal: I venture to say the court should not act thus.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say the court should not act in this way.

sentences.zh: 」後怒曰：「何謂魁首？

translations.literal: The empress angrily said: "What is meant by ringleader?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said angrily, "What do you mean by ringleader?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「魁者，大帥；

translations.literal: He answered: "Kui means great commander;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Kui means the great commander;

sentences.zh: 首者，元謀。

translations.literal: shou means prime plotter."
translations.idiomatic: shou means the prime plotter."

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「餘慶安得不為魁首？

translations.literal: The empress said: "How can Yuqing not be the ringleader?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "How can Yuqing not be the ringleader?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「若魁首者，虺貞是已。

translations.literal: He answered: "If there is a ringleader, it is Hui Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If there is a ringleader, it is Hui Zhen."

sentences.zh: 既已伏誅，餘慶今方論罪，非支黨何？

translations.literal: Since they have already been executed, Yuqing is now only being judged for his crime—if not a branch follower, what is he?
translations.idiomatic: Since they have already been executed, Yuqing is only now being judged for his crime—if he is not a branch follower, what is he?

sentences.zh: 」後意解，乃曰：「公更思之。

translations.literal: The empress's mind eased and she said: "Sir, think again."
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mind eased and she said, "Sir, think again."

sentences.zh: 」遂免死。

translations.literal: He was then spared death.
translations.idiomatic: He was then spared from death.

sentences.zh: 當此時，左右及衛仗在廷陛者數百人，皆縮項不敢息，而有功氣定言詳，然不橈。

translations.literal: At this time the attendants left and right and the guard troops on the court steps numbered in the hundreds; all shrank their necks and dared not breathe, yet Yougong's bearing was calm and his words measured, and he did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the attendants at left and right and the guard troops on the court steps numbered in the hundreds; all shrank their necks and dared not breathe, yet Yougong's bearing was calm, his words measured, and he did not bend.

sentences.zh: 有韓紀孝者，受徐敬業偽官，前已物故，推事使顧仲琰籍其家，詔已報可。

translations.literal: There was one Han Jixiao who had accepted a false office from Xu Jingye and had previously died. The commissioner of investigation Gu Zhongyan was registering his household; the edict had already reported approval.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Han Jixiao who had accepted a false office from Xu Jingye and had already died. The commissioner of investigation Gu Zhongyan was registering his household, and the edict had already reported approval.

sentences.zh: 有功追議曰：「律，謀反者斬。

translations.literal: Yougong pursued deliberation and said: "In the code, those who plot rebellion are beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Yougong pursued deliberation and said, "In the code, those who plot rebellion are beheaded."

sentences.zh: 身亡即無斬法，無斬法則不得相緣。

translations.literal: When the body is dead there is no beheading statute; without a beheading statute there can be no successive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the person is dead there is no statute for beheading; without a statute for beheading there can be no successive punishment.

sentences.zh: 所緣之人亡，則所因之罪減。

translations.literal: When the person connected to the chain is dead, the crime from which it derives is reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When the person connected in the chain is dead, the crime from which it derives is reduced.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，皆以更赦免，如此獲宥者數十百姓。

translations.literal: The edict followed him; all were spared through the next amnesty—thus several tens of families gained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed his view; all were spared through the next amnesty—thus several tens of families gained pardon.

sentences.zh: 累轉秋官郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Autumn Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to director of the autumn office.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎任知古、冬官尚書裴行本等七人被誣當死，後謂宰相曰：「古人以殺止殺，我今以恩止殺，就群公丐知古等，賜以再生，可乎？

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Director Ren Zhigu, Minister of Winter Works Pei Xingben, and seven others were falsely accused and should die. The empress said to the chancellor: "The ancients stopped killing with killing; I today will stop killing with grace. From you gentlemen I beg Zhigu and the rest—grant them rebirth—is it possible?"
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix pavilion vice director Ren Zhigu, minister of winter works Pei Xingben, and seven others were falsely accused and condemned to death. The empress said to the chancellor, "The ancients stopped killing with killing; I today will stop killing with grace. From you gentlemen I beg Zhigu and the rest—grant them rebirth—is that possible?"

sentences.zh: 」俊臣、張知默固請如法，後不許。

translations.literal: Junchen and Zhang Zhimuo firmly requested according to law; the empress did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen and Zhang Zhimuo firmly requested execution according to law, but the empress would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 俊臣獨引行本更驗前罪。

translations.literal: Junchen alone drew Xingben back to verify prior crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen alone drew Xingben back to verify prior crimes.

sentences.zh: 有功奏曰：「俊臣違陛下再生之賜，不可以示信。

translations.literal: Yougong memorialized: "Junchen violates Your Majesty's gift of rebirth and may not be shown as trustworthy."
translations.idiomatic: Yougong memorialized, "Junchen violates Your Majesty's gift of rebirth and cannot be shown as trustworthy."

sentences.zh: 」於是悉免死。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were spared from death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all were spared from death.

sentences.zh: 道州刺史李仁褒兄弟為人誣構，有功爭不能得。

translations.literal: The prefect of Dao Prefecture Li Renbao and his brothers were falsely framed by others; Yougong disputed but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Dao Prefecture Li Renbao and his brothers were falsely framed by others; Yougong disputed on their behalf but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 秋官侍郎周興劾之曰：「漢法，附下罔上者斬，面欺者亦斬。

translations.literal: Autumn Office Vice Director Zhou Xing impeached him: "Han law: those who attach below and deceive above are beheaded; those who deceive the face are also beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Autumn office vice director Zhou Xing impeached him, saying, "Han law: those who attach below and deceive above are beheaded; those who deceive to one's face are also beheaded."

sentences.zh: 在古，析言破律者殺。

translations.literal: In antiquity, those who split words to break the code were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, those who split words to break the code were killed.

sentences.zh: 有功故出反囚，罪當誅，請按之。

translations.literal: Yougong deliberately released treason prisoners; the crime merits execution—I request investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong deliberately released treason prisoners; the crime merits execution—I request investigation.

sentences.zh: 」後不許，猶坐史官。

translations.literal: The empress did not permit it, but he still suffered reduction as a history official.
translations.idiomatic: The empress did not permit it, but he still suffered demotion as a history official.

sentences.zh: 俄起為左肅政臺侍御史，辭曰：「臣聞鹿走山林而命系庖廚者，勢固自然。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised as Attending Censor of the Left Office for Scrutinizing Government; he declined: "Your servant has heard that when a deer runs in mountain forests yet its life is tied to the kitchen, the tendency is of itself so."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was raised as attending censor of the left office for scrutinizing government, but he declined, saying, "Your servant has heard that when a deer runs in mountain forests yet its life is tied to the kitchen, the tendency is of itself so."

sentences.zh: 陛下以法官用臣，臣守正行法，必坐此死矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty employs your servant as a judge; your servant keeps to the upright and executes the law—I am certain to die for this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty employs your servant as a judge; your servant keeps to the upright and executes the law—I am certain to die for this.

sentences.zh: 」後固授之。

translations.literal: The empress firmly appointed him anyway.
translations.idiomatic: The empress firmly appointed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 天下聞有功復進，灑然相賀。

translations.literal: When all under Heaven heard Yougong had been promoted again, they rejoiced together in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When all under Heaven heard that Yougong had been promoted again, they rejoiced together in relief.

sentences.zh: 時有詔：「公坐流、私坐徒以上會赦免，逾百日不首者，復論。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict: "For public crimes punished by exile and private crimes punished by hard labor and above, meeting an amnesty grants exemption; those who do not confess past one hundred days are prosecuted again."
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was an edict: "For public crimes punished by exile and private crimes punished by hard labor and above, meeting an amnesty grants exemption; those who do not confess within one hundred days are prosecuted again."

sentences.zh: 」有功奏曰：「陛下寬殊死罪，已發者原之，是通改過之心、自新之路。

translations.literal: Yougong memorialized: "Your Majesty has eased extraordinary death sentences and forgives those already exposed—that opens the mind to reform wrongdoing and the road to renewal."
translations.idiomatic: Yougong memorialized, "Your Majesty has eased extraordinary death sentences and forgives those already exposed—that opens the mind to reform wrongdoing and the road to renewal."

sentences.zh: 故律，告赦前事，以其罪坐之。

translations.literal: Therefore in the code, reporting pre-amnesty matters assigns guilt according to the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the code, reporting pre-amnesty matters assigns guilt according to the crime.

sentences.zh: 若無告言，所犯終不自發；

translations.literal: If there is no report, the offense in the end will not expose itself;
translations.idiomatic: If there is no report, the offense in the end will not expose itself;

sentences.zh: 如告言赦前事，則與律乖。

translations.literal: if one reports pre-amnesty matters, it clashes with the code.
translations.idiomatic: if one reports pre-amnesty matters, it clashes with the code.

sentences.zh: 今赦前之罪，不自言者，還以法論，即恩雖布天下，而一罪不能貸，臣竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: Now pre-amnesty crimes for those who do not speak themselves are still judged by law—then though grace is spread over all under Heaven, a single crime cannot be remitted; your servant ventures that Your Majesty should not take this course.
translations.idiomatic: Now pre-amnesty crimes for those who do not confess themselves are still judged by law—then though grace is spread over all under Heaven, a single crime cannot be remitted. Your servant ventures that Your Majesty should not take this course.

sentences.zh: 」後更詔五品以上議可。

translations.literal: The empress then ordered officials of the fifth rank and above to deliberate approval.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then ordered officials of the fifth rank and above to deliberate and approve.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：「天下員有定，比選者日多，選曹諉囑公行，囂謗滿路。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial: "Empire-wide posts have a fixed count, yet daily the candidates for selection grow; the Selection Bureau shrugs off duties publicly, and clamor and slander fill the roads."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial, saying, "Empire-wide posts have a fixed count, yet daily the candidates for selection grow. The selection bureau shrugs off its duties in public, and clamor and slander fill the roads."

sentences.zh: 唐季人多逆節，鞫訊結斷，刑慘獄嚴，革命歲久，其流弗改。

translations.literal: In the late Tang many men turned against propriety; interrogation and closing of cases—the punishments cruel, the prisons severe. Since the revolution many years have passed, yet the drift has not changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the troubled close of Tang many men turned against propriety. Interrogation and closing of cases—the punishments were cruel and the prisons severe. Since the revolution many years have passed, yet the drift has not changed.

sentences.zh: 事表生情，法外構理，而刻薄吏驅扇成奸。

translations.literal: Matters show emotion on the surface; outside the code they construct reasoning, while harsh petty officials drive and fan them into treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Matters show emotion on the surface; outside the code they construct reasoning, while harsh petty officials drive and fan them into treachery.

sentences.zh: 雖朝堂進表，列匭內牒，叫閽弗聽，叩鼓弗聞，使申其冤，正增其枉。

translations.literal: Though they advance memorials in the court hall, file dispatches in the letter box, cry at the gate and be not heard, beat the drum and be not heeded—if they are allowed to state their wrongs, they only add to their injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Though they advance memorials in the court hall, file petitions in the accusation box, cry at the gate and go unheard, beat the drum and go unheeded—if they are allowed to state their grievances, they only add to their injustice.

sentences.zh: 誠令天官銓註有所不平、法司推斷舞法深詆、三司理匭受所上章擁塞不白者皆許臣按驗劾發，奪祿貶勞，不越月逾時，可致刑措。

translations.literal: If it is truly ordered that wherever the Heavenly Office's selection and annotation is unfair, wherever the judicial offices' judgments twist the law in deep slander, and wherever the Three Offices' petition box receives memorials that are blocked and not reported—all are permitted to your servant to investigate, verify, impeach, and expose, stripping salary and demoting to labor, within no more than a month or season, punishments may be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly permits me to investigate and impeach wherever the heavenly office's selections are unfair, wherever judicial offices twist the law in deep calumny, and wherever the three offices' petition box blocks memorials from being reported—stripping salaries and demoting offenders to labor service—then within a month or season punishments may be set aside altogether.

sentences.zh: 」後納之。

translations.literal: The empress accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 竇孝諶妻龐為其奴怖以妖祟，教為夜解，因告以厭詛。

translations.literal: Pang, wife of Dou Xiaochen, was frightened by her slave with talk of demonic portents; the slave taught her night rituals of release and then reported her for curse-magic.
translations.idiomatic: Pang, wife of Dou Xiaochen, was frightened by her slave with talk of demonic portents. The slave taught her night rituals of release and then reported her for practicing curse-magic.

sentences.zh: 給事中薛季昶鞫之，龐當死。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xue Jichang interrogated the case; Pang was liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xue Jichang interrogated the case, and Pang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 子希瑊訟冤，有功明其枉。

translations.literal: Her son Xizhen sued over the injustice; Yougong showed she had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Xizhen appealed the injustice, and Yougong showed that she had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 季昶劾有功黨惡逆，當棄市。

translations.literal: Jichang impeached Yougong as partisan to wicked rebellion; he should be executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang impeached Yougong as partisan to wicked rebellion and demanded he be executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 有功方視事，令史泣以告。

translations.literal: Yougong was just attending to business when a clerk wept and told him.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong was just attending to business when a clerk came weeping to tell him.

sentences.zh: 有功曰：「豈吾獨死，而諸人長不死邪？

translations.literal: Yougong said: "How is it that I alone should die while all others live long and do not die?"
translations.idiomatic: Yougong said, "How is it that I alone should die while all others live on?"

sentences.zh: 」安步去。

translations.literal: He walked away at an easy pace.
translations.idiomatic: He walked away at an easy pace.

sentences.zh: 後召詰曰：「公比斷獄多失出，何耶？

translations.literal: The empress summoned and questioned him: "Sir, of late in judging cases you often err on the side of release—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress summoned and questioned him, saying, "Sir, of late in judging cases you often err on the side of release—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「失出，臣小過；

translations.literal: He answered: "Erring on release is your servant's small fault;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Erring on the side of release is your servant's small fault;

sentences.zh: 好生，陛下大德。

translations.literal: cherishing life is Your Majesty's great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: cherishing life is Your Majesty's great virtue."

sentences.zh: 」後默然。

translations.literal: The empress was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress fell silent.

sentences.zh: 龐得減死，有功免為民。

translations.literal: Pang's death was reduced; Yougong was spared and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Pang's sentence was reduced from death, and Yougong was spared and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 起拜左司郎中，轉司刑少卿。

translations.literal: He was raised and appointed Director of the Left Bureau; transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised and appointed director of the left bureau, then transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 與皇甫文備同按獄，誣有功縱逆黨。

translations.literal: Together with Huangfu Wenbei he reviewed cases and falsely accused Yougong of releasing rebel partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Huangfu Wenbei he reviewed cases and falsely accused Yougong of releasing rebel partisans.

sentences.zh: 久之，文備坐事下獄，有功出之。

translations.literal: After a long while Wenbei was implicated and cast into prison; Yougong released him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenbei was implicated and cast into prison, and Yougong secured his release.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「彼嘗陷君於死，今生之，何也？

translations.literal: Someone said: "He once trapped you in death; now you give him life—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "He once tried to have you killed—why do you now save his life?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「爾所言者私忿，我所守者公法，不可以私害公。」

translations.literal: He answered: "What you speak of is private resentment; what I uphold is public law—private feeling must not harm the public good."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "What you speak of is private resentment; what I uphold is public law—private feeling must not harm the public good."

sentences.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「大理，人命所系，不可阿旨詭辭，以求茍免。

translations.literal: He once said to those close to him: "The Court of Review is where human lives are bound; one must not bend to intent with twisted words to seek a shabby escape."
translations.idiomatic: He once said to those close to him, "The court of review is where human lives are bound. One must not bend to intent with twisted words merely to seek a shabby escape."

sentences.zh: 」故有功為獄，常持平守正，以執據冤罔，凡三坐大辟，將死，泰然不憂，赦之，亦不喜，後以此重之。

translations.literal: Therefore in handling prisons Yougong constantly held the balance and kept to the upright, grasping the basis of wrongful imprisonment. Three times he was liable to the great punishment; facing death he was calm and untroubled, and when pardoned he was not glad—the empress thereafter valued him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in handling prisons Yougong constantly held the balance and kept to the upright, seizing on the basis of wrongful imprisonment. Three times he was liable to capital punishment; facing death he was calm and untroubled, and when pardoned he was not glad. The empress thereafter valued him all the more for this.

sentences.zh: 所全活甚眾，酷吏為少衰，然疾之如仇矣。

translations.literal: Those he preserved alive were very many; harsh officials somewhat declined, yet they hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The number he preserved alive was very great, and harsh officials somewhat declined, yet they hated him as an enemy.

sentences.zh: 改司仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the court of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈司刑卿。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-eight; posthumously given Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，加贈越州都督，遣使就第吊祭，賜物百段，授一子官。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne he was further posthumously made Military Governor of Yuezhou; envoys were sent to his residence for mourning sacrifice, a hundred lengths of goods were granted, and one son was given office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne he was further posthumously made military governor of Yuezhou. Envoys were sent to his residence for mourning sacrifices, a hundred lengths of goods were granted, and one son was given office.

sentences.zh: 開元初，竇希瑊等請以己官讓有功子惀，以報舊德，由是自大理司直遷恭陵令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Dou Xizhen and others requested to yield their own offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of old kindness; thereby he rose from Straight Officer of the Court of Review to Magistrate of Gong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era Dou Xizhen and others asked to yield their own offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of his old kindness. Thereby Lun rose from straight officer of the court of review to magistrate of Gong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，追謚忠正。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he was posthumously titled Loyal and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era he was posthumously titled Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 初，鹿城主簿潘好禮慕有功為人，論之曰：「昔稱張釋之為廷尉，天下無冤人，今有功斷獄，亦天下無冤人。

translations.literal: Initially Pan Haoli, chief clerk of Lucheng, admired Yougong's character and discussed him, saying: "In the past Zhang Shizhi as Court Commandant was said to leave the realm without wronged men; now Yougong in judging cases also leaves the realm without wronged men."
translations.idiomatic: Initially Pan Haoli, chief clerk of Lucheng, admired Yougong's character and said, "In the past Zhang Shizhi as court commandant was said to leave the realm without wronged men; now Yougong in judging cases also leaves the realm without wronged men."

sentences.zh: 然釋之當漢文帝時，中外無事，守法而已。

translations.literal: Yet Shizhi was in the time of Emperor Wen of Han, when within and without there was no trouble—he merely kept the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shizhi served under Emperor Wen of Han, when within and without the realm was at peace—he merely kept the law.

sentences.zh: 有功居革命之際，周興、來俊臣等掩義隱賊，崇飾惡言，以誣盛德，有功守死明道，身濱殆者數矣，此其賢於釋之明甚。

translations.literal: Yougong dwelt in the time of revolution; Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen and others covered righteousness and hid villainy, exalting and adorning evil words to slander great virtue. Yougong held to death in the bright Way; his person neared peril several times—here his worth exceeds Shizhi's, and clearly so.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong lived in an age of revolution, when Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others covered righteousness and hid villainy, exalting evil words to slander great virtue. Yougong held to death in defense of the bright Way and several times came to the brink of peril—here his worth clearly far exceeds Shizhi's.

sentences.zh: 」或稱有功仁恕過漢於、張。

translations.literal: Some called Yougong's benevolence and forbearance superior to the Han officials Yu and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Yougong's benevolence and forbearance surpassed those of the Han officials Yu Ding and Zhang Tang.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人盧若虛曰：「徐公當雷霆之震，而能全仁恕，雖千載未見其比。

translations.literal: Diarist Lu Ruoxu said: "Lord Xu faced the thunder's shock yet could preserve benevolence and forbearance whole—though a thousand years have passed, his like has not been seen."
translations.idiomatic: Diarist Lu Ruoxu said, "Lord Xu faced the thunderbolt's shock yet preserved benevolence and forbearance whole—in a thousand years his like has not been seen."

sentences.zh: 」五世孫商。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation descendant was Shang.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation descendant was Shang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「徐有功不以唐、周貳其心，惟一於法，身蹈死以救人之死，故能處猜後、酷吏之間，以恕自將，內挫虐焰，不使天下殘於燎，可謂仁人也哉！

translations.literal: The encomium says: "Xu Yougong did not divide his heart between Tang and Zhou—he was single-minded in the law, himself treading death to save others from death. Thus he could dwell between a suspicious empress and harsh officials, taking forbearance as his guide, inwardly blunting the flame of cruelty so that the realm was not maimed by the blaze—he may be called a man of benevolence!"
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says, "Xu Yougong did not divide his heart between Tang and Zhou—he was single-minded in the law and himself trod death to save others from death. Thus he could dwell between a suspicious empress and harsh officials, taking forbearance as his guide, inwardly blunting the flame of cruelty so that the realm was not maimed by the blaze. He may truly be called a man of benevolence!"

sentences.zh: 議者謂過漢於、張，渠不信夫！

translations.literal: Those who discuss say he surpassed the Han officials Yu and Zhang—how can one not believe it!
translations.idiomatic: Commentators say he surpassed the Han officials Yu and Zhang—how can one not believe it!

sentences.zh: 商，字義聲，或字秋卿，客新鄭再世，因為新鄭人。

translations.literal: Shang, style name Yisheng or also Qiuqing, guest in Xinzheng for two generations—thus he became a man of Xinzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shang, whose style name was Yisheng or also Qiuqing, had been a guest in Xinzheng for two generations and thus came to be regarded as a man of Xinzheng.

sentences.zh: 幼隱中條山。

translations.literal: In youth he lived in seclusion on Zhongtiao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived in seclusion on Zhongtiao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He was elevated to the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中時，擢累尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he was repeatedly promoted to left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣宗詔為巡邊使，使有指，拜河中節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered him as frontier inspection commissioner; when the mission had purpose he was appointed Military Commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong appointed him frontier inspection commissioner, and when his mission proved successful he was made military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 突厥殘種保特峨山，以千帳度河自歸，詔商綏定。

translations.literal: Remnant Turks held Mount E; with a thousand tents they crossed the river to submit of themselves, and an edict ordered Shang to pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant Turks held Mount E. With a thousand tents they crossed the river to submit voluntarily, and an edict ordered Shang to pacify and settle them.

sentences.zh: 商表處山東寬鄉，置備征軍，凡千人，襞紙為鎧，勁矢不能洞。

translations.literal: Shang memorialized to place them in broad townships east of the mountains, establishing a reserve expeditionary army of a thousand men; they folded paper as armor, and strong arrows could not pierce it.
translations.idiomatic: Shang memorialized to settle them in broad townships east of the mountains and established a reserve expeditionary army of a thousand men who folded paper into armor that even strong arrows could not pierce.

sentences.zh: 徙節山南東道，襄多山棚，為票賊，商取材卒為捕盜將，別為屯營，寇所發，輒跡捕，捕必得，遂為精兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Shannan East Circuit; Xiang had many mountain stockades who became fierce bandits. Shang selected able soldiers as bandit-capture generals and set up separate encampments; wherever bandits struck he traced and seized them, capture was certain, and they became elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Shannan East Circuit. Xiang had many mountain stockade communities who became fierce bandits. Shang selected able soldiers as bandit-capture generals and set up separate encampments; wherever bandits struck he traced and seized them, capture was certain, and they became elite troops.

sentences.zh: 江西都將反，韋宙乘傳抵山南發兵，商命部將韓季友以捕盜營士往。

translations.literal: A chief general of Jiangxi rebelled; Wei Zhou took relay post-horses to Shannan to raise troops, and Shang ordered his subordinate general Han Jiyou to go with the bandit-capture camp soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: A chief general of Jiangxi rebelled. Wei Zhou took relay post-horses to Shannan to raise troops, and Shang ordered his subordinate general Han Jiyou to go with the bandit-capture camp soldiers.

sentences.zh: 賊平，宙表留季友所部為綱紀。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Zhou memorialized to retain Jiyou's command as local discipline force.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, Zhou memorialized to retain Jiyou's command as a local discipline force.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，以刑部尚書為諸道鹽鐵轉運使，封東莞縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong, as Minister of Punishments he was made Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner for all circuits and enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongguan County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiantong era, as minister of punishments he was made salt and iron transport commissioner for all circuits and enfeoffed as viscount of Dongguan County.

sentences.zh: 四年，進同中書門下平章事，出為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery and sent out as Military Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was advanced to associate director of the secretariat and chancellery and sent out as military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 累進太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly advanced to grand guardian of the heir apparent and died.

sentences.zh: 子彥若，事僖宗為中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Yanruo served Xizong as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanruo served Emperor Xizong as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 昭宗立，再用為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong took the throne he was again used as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne he was again appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 張浚師敗太原，以彥若為戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun's army was defeated at Taiyuan, Yanruo was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun's army was defeated at Taiyuan, Yanruo was made vice minister of revenue and associate director of the secretariat and chancellery.

sentences.zh: 俄代李茂貞為鳳翔節度使，不得入，還為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Li Maozhen as Military Commissioner of Fengxiang but could not enter; he returned as Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Li Maozhen as military commissioner of Fengxiang but could not take up the post and returned as grand censor.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，復當國，進位太保、齊國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he again held the state, advanced to Grand Guardian and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianning era he again held power, advanced to grand guardian and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 崔胤專政，以彥若位己右，不悅，以平章事為清海軍節度使，卒於鎮，而行軍司馬劉隱因主留務。

translations.literal: Cui Yin monopolized government; because Yanruo stood above him he was displeased and made him Military Commissioner of Qinghai Army as grand councillor; he died in the command, and the army marching marshal Liu Yin thereby took charge of remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin monopolized government and, displeased that Yanruo outranked him, sent him out as military commissioner of the Qinghai army while retaining his grand councillor title. Yanruo died in the command, and the army marching marshal Liu Yin thereby took charge of remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 方時多難，彥若最見信於帝，有以事自陳者，帝曰：「汝當問彥若。

translations.literal: In that time of many troubles Yanruo was most trusted by the emperor; when someone presented a matter on his own behalf the emperor said: "You should ask Yanruo."
translations.idiomatic: In that troubled age Yanruo was most trusted by the emperor. When someone presented a matter on his own behalf the emperor said, "You should ask Yanruo."

sentences.zh: 」其所倚任如此。

translations.literal: Such was the reliance and trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the reliance the emperor placed in him.
